question: advisor round-5 point 7b: physics-informed vs data-driven training principle
metric: per-component relative L2 on the held-out set, Tables 5/11's definition

physics_informed.optimizer: Adam lr=2e-3 wd=0.0, x0.9 every 1000 epochs

data_driven_matched_optimizer.optimizer: Adam lr=2e-3 wd=0.0, matched to the PI run
data_driven_matched_optimizer.note: the clean comparison: only the loss differs

data_driven_own_optimizer.note: confounded: a better optimizer AND a different loss. Best was the FINAL step, so it had not converged -- 0.0826 is a lower bound on this recipe, not its ceiling.

physics_informed_adamw_onecycle.optimizer: AdamW lr=1e-3 wd=1e-5 + OneCycleLR over 75,000 steps
physics_informed_adamw_onecycle.recipe_verified: VERIFIED against the command actually run: --optimizer adamw_onecycle --onecycle_total_steps 75000 --lr 1e-3 --weight_decay 1e-5 --ntrain 800 --ntest 200 --batch_size 8 --epochs 750. 800/8 = 100 steps per epoch x 750 epochs = 75,000 steps, matching every other run in the table, and lr/wd match the data-driven run's recipe exactly. The AdamW column is therefore a clean loss-only comparison.
physics_informed_adamw_onecycle.minor_caveat: --validate_every was not passed, so this run validated every 10 epochs (75 events) while the physics-informed Adam run used 25 (30 events). More validation events give more chances to catch a lucky minimum. The effect here is negligible: best 0.1247 against final 0.1258, a gap of 0.9%, so the reported best is not a fluctuation.

findings.matched: under the same optimizer the physics-informed model is 36% more accurate (0.0959 vs 0.1307). The data-driven advantage seen in the first run came from the optimizer, not the loss.
findings.unmatched: each under its own preferred recipe, the data-driven model is 16% more accurate (0.0826 vs 0.0959).
findings.label_cost: the data-driven model additionally requires 800 FEM solves = 5.65 h of CPU at Table 4a's measured rate, which the physics-informed model does not pay at all. This is independent of the optimizer.
findings.the_2x2_is_complete: By column, isolating the LOSS at a matched optimizer and a matched 75,000-step budget: under Adam 2e-3 the physics-informed loss wins by 26.6% (0.0959 vs 0.1307); under AdamW lr=1e-3 wd=1e-5 + OneCycleLR the data-driven loss wins by 33.8% (0.1247 vs 0.0826). THE RANKING FLIPS WITH THE OPTIMIZER. Neither training principle wins outright, and the report says exactly that.
findings.the_optimizer_affects_the_two_losses_in_: AdamW+OneCycleLR makes the physics-informed model 30.0% WORSE (0.0959 -> 0.1247) and the data-driven model 36.8% BETTER (0.1307 -> 0.0826). That is the mechanism behind the flip: a schedule tuned on one loss is not neutral ground for the other.
findings.label_cost_is_unaffected: Independently of the optimizer, the data-driven model needs 800 FEM solves = 5.65 h of CPU for its labels; the physics-informed one needs none. This is the one claim in the comparison that does not depend on the recipe.
